description:
The report's item-link pass reports a `<short-id>/<self-id>` link label as dangling when the self-id matches the id pattern of more than one issue-scoped item kind, although the item exists and the executor resolves it.

## Background

- `ItemAddressIndex::contains` (`crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs`) expands a sugar address through `expand_sugar_address`, which picks the kind by matching the self-id against each issue-scoped kind's id pattern and fails with `ItemError::SugarKindAmbiguous` when several match (`item.rs:422-438`).
- The executor's link resolution (`resolve_link_label` → `show_item`, `crates/jit/src/commands/item.rs:347,559`) resolves the same labels, so the two disagree.
- A report test written for c1af05ac shows it: with the item kinds `invariant`, `requirement`, `decision` and `risk` declared, `per:<short>/D-01` and `mitigates:<short>/RISK-01` on an issue whose description declares `D-01` and `RISK-01` are reported as dangling by the report and resolved by the executor.
- The report reached this path with the item-address index (001a9c46); repository validation and every view built on the report inherit it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The report resolves a `<short-id>/<self-id>` link label to the item it names whenever exactly one item exists at that address under the issue-scoped kinds the self-id's pattern admits, and reports it as dangling only when no such item exists or more than one does.
- [hard] REQ-02: The report and the executor's link resolution agree on every link label in the existing item-link tests, including the `per:` and `mitigates:` sugar labels above.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests over the address index show a sugar address resolving when its self-id matches several kinds' patterns but one item exists, and staying dangling when none exists.

## Notes

- Found while relocating the executor-pass tests (c1af05ac), whose report suite cannot pass until this is fixed.
title: Item links resolve sugar addresses whose self-id several kinds admit
